_comment: Tenant registry — the single source of truth for both backends:
The server, never the client, owns anything with money attached:
which Toast locations a tenant has, the earn rate, and reward costs.
Secrets are NOT here. Each tenant names the env vars holding its
credentials; values come from `wrangler secret put <NAME>` or .env.
Adding a restaurant is a new entry here plus its secrets. No code changes.

soco.name: Southern Comfort Kitchen
soco._origins: Browsers allowed to call this tenant's API. localhost is always permitted for development.
soco._locations: Toast restaurant GUIDs. Not secret — they appear in public ordering URLs. null = not in this credential set yet.
_allowlist: SOFT LAUNCH GATE. Launch runs without SMS verification, so a phone
number is the only thing identifying a guest. Only numbers listed here
can earn or redeem — an unenrolled number gets nothing, so guessing a
number gains an attacker nothing unless it is already enrolled.
10 digits, no punctuation. [] means nobody (fails closed).
Set to null to open enrolment to everyone — only once OTP is live.
soco._earn: pointsPerDollar x item price. See LAUNCH.local.md (gitignored) for the measured average ticket and points per visit.
soco._lookbackDays: Used only by backend/backfill.py for the one-time history import. The cron sync walks forward from its own cursor.
_rewards: Calibrated July 2026 against the measured Castro Valley average
ticket (see LAUNCH.local.md, gitignored). First reward lands at about
3 visits; blended giveback ~2.5-4%, against a restaurant-loyalty norm
of 2-5%. The previous ladder put the first reward 7+ visits out at
~1.2%, which most guests would never have reached.
Costs here are authoritative. The app displays them but the server
prices every redemption from this table.

rewards.name: Brill Brothers' Table — feast for 4 + merch
